approach: Grep for repeated structural patterns — same validation block, same SQL query in N services, same compute logic across components, same string constants embedded inline.

patterns_found.title: menuRoleAdjustedAddonPrice duplicated across PricingService and CompositionSnapshotBuilder
patterns_found.body_similarity: ~99% identical — same role match, same ratio defaults from config('kiosk.menu_pricing'), same fallback to 1.0
patterns_found.documented_reason: CompositionSnapshotBuilder header comment: 'kept local to keep the snapshot builder a pure transformer (no PricingService dep). Any drift here would be an NF525 audit-chain mismatch'
patterns_found.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS — frozen-zone-adjacent NF525 critical path. Pulling into a shared trait or static helper would require refactoring CompositionSnapshotBuilder's purity contract. Risk > value.
patterns_found.user_friendly: The same 20-line price-ratio calculation is in two files on purpose. It is a fiscal-law-critical (NF525) computation, and the dev team chose to copy it rather than share it to avoid a hidden dependency. Don't touch — it works and a refactor could violate fiscal audit chain rules.

patterns_found.title: BranchScope::withoutGlobalScope bypass pattern (~13 call sites)
locations: Pre-auth login lookups in controllers, admin cross-branch queries, fiscal allocation lookups
patterns_found.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS — each call site is auditable and security-critical. Encapsulation into a helper would obscure the security boundary. The 13 sites are each accompanied by a comment explaining why scope is bypassed.
patterns_found.user_friendly: There is a small repeated pattern (~13 places) where the system asks the database 'ignore the branch filter for this query'. Each instance is documented. Hiding it behind a helper function would actually make the security audit harder. Keep visible.

patterns_found.title: Cache::lock(...)->block(3, ...) concurrency pattern (3+ services)
patterns_found.body_similarity: Same Cache::lock(key, 5)->block(3, fn) shape, different keys and bodies
patterns_found.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS — pattern only, not body duplicate. Extracting to a `LockedTransaction` helper is a nice refactor but no business value gain.
patterns_found.user_friendly: Three places use the same 'briefly lock so two requests don't fight' pattern. The 5-second-lock / 3-second-wait shape is repeated but the keys and the protected work differ. Looks like discipline, not duplication.

patterns_found.title: PricingService calls (27 sites across app/) — high coupling but no body duplicate
patterns_found.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS — PricingService is the SSOT (single source of truth, per CLAUDE.md §8 NF525) for prices. Every site that touches money goes through it — by design.
patterns_found.user_friendly: Twenty-seven different places call the central PricingService for price math. That is the intended design (one source of truth for money). Not a duplication.

patterns_found.title: FormRequest validation rules — Bkash.php Requests folder vs PaymentRequests folder
patterns_found.body_similarity: Class name identical; rules() body different; Requests/* has real validation, PaymentRequests/* are empty stubs (spot-check: Cashfree/Razorpay/Senangpay all return [] — only Stripe stub has 1 rule)
patterns_found.intentional: UNCONFIRMED — the empty-stub pattern may be intentional (downstream gateway services validate) or unfinished work
patterns_found.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS — runtime depends on both folders existing; deleting breaks payment. But OWNER SHOULD CONFIRM the empty-stub pattern is intended design.
patterns_found.user_friendly: See duplicate-files.json #1. Twin folders per payment provider. Admin side validates real fields. Customer side returns empty rules (Stripe is the exception with one rule). Worth a quick owner sanity-check — is the empty-stub pattern on purpose?

patterns_NOT_found: No N-service-with-same-SQL-query duplications detected — services are well-encapsulated
No copy-paste FormRequest rule blocks across controllers (other than PATTERN-5 above)
